title: Billy Phillips killed: Easter Monday shooting and 50 cent wages
summary: He tells of Gyp the Blood killing Billy Phillips and the Parkers' successors, the district closing, and wages of 50 cents a night.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah, I never heard talk of Buddy Ford though. I don't know who that is.

Frank Early was a nightclub owner too. And he lived. It was during the time that his short life of Gypsy Blood killed Billy Phillips. I was playing at Billy Phillips. I was playing at Billy Phillips the other night that played for Billy Phillips. The other night Gypsy Blood killed Billy Phillips. I just got paid. The 20 minutes after, that was Easter Monday. I got paid the 20 minutes after Billy Phillips was killed. He was killed at, let's see, at 4 o'clock. And we got paid 20 minutes after 4. If we hadn't got paid that night, well if we hadn't got paid that night, now we would have got paid. Maybe because the whole district closed down right there and then. He was the one that was the strongest business across Canal Street. A man called Billy Phillips. You heard talk of him?

Yeah, he's right. That's right. Charlie Parker was his brother. No, Charlie Parker had the place after Billy Phillips lost it. Charlie Parker and Harry Parker. And that same night, while the band had knocked off, we all got knocked off and got paid. In those days, the only gift of men, oh I hate to tell you the wages. Wages, ramping down the corner, 50 cents a night. First of all, I pay 50 cents a night. Wages, 50 cents a night. Or tips you could make. Show you the difference in this town now. 50 cents a night. And wake down there at Old Archie Cafe. A corner and Burgundy. 50 cents a night. And tips. But 50 cents was worth more than $2 then. It was more than two and a half. At that time. Yeah.
